meta.title: Lag compensation
meta.subtitle: A tick-indexed ring of collision worlds, and the delay measurement that selects a slot

views.label: The delay measurement
views.note: The client measures how far behind it is rendering and ships that number in every command.

views.label: The history ring
views.note: One collision world clone per full tick, stored at tick modulo size, tagged with its tick.

views.label: The rewind query
views.note: Compare expected tick with returned tick, or clamping will fail silently forever.

nodes.label: Rewind query
nodes.sublabel: clamps, reports the tick it gave

cards.title: Why the server cannot guess the delay
items: Interpolation delay depends on the client's own jitter and window settings
So the client measures it and writes it into every command packet
The server stores it per connection and copies it onto the owned ghost
It is only refreshed when a command arrives for that specific entity

cards.title: The ring is a direct-mapped cache
items: Index is the low bits of the tick, which is why the size must be a power of two
The tick is stored alongside the slot and acts as the tag
A read hands back the tick it actually found
Requests older than the ring are clamped to the oldest slot, not refused

cards.title: The silent failure
items: The short overload throws away expected tick and returned tick
A high-latency client then gets the oldest world forever, with no signal
Compare the two ticks and log the mismatch
That comparison is how you learn your history is too short

cards.title: Somebody absorbs the latency
items: The server rewinds the target, not the shooter and not the level
So a player can be hit after their own screen shows them behind cover
Without compensation the shooter absorbs it instead, by leading every target
The interpolation window and the history size are the two bounds you control
